7077-we-can-t-have-everything-a-novel.title: We Can T Have Everything A Novel
7077-we-can-t-have-everything-a-novel.creator: Rupert Hughes
7077-we-can-t-have-everything-a-novel.description: A book by Rupert Hughes. Jim Dyckman, infamously rich (through no fault of his own), could not see far enough past Charity Coe Cheever that day to make out Kedzie Thropp, a few seats removed. Charity Coe--most of Mrs. Cheever's friends still called her by her maiden name--sat with her back turned to Kedzie; and latterly Charity Coe was not looking over her shoulder much. She did not see Kedzie at all.

arxiv-2005-07886.title: Integrating Semantic and Structural Information with Graph Convolutional Network for Controversy Detection
arxiv-2005-07886.creator: Lei Zhong, Juan Cao, Qiang Sheng, Junbo Guo, Ziang Wang
arxiv-2005-07886.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Lei Zhong, Juan Cao, Qiang Sheng, Junbo Guo, Ziang Wang. Identifying controversial posts on social media is a fundamental task for mining public sentiment, assessing the influence of events, and alleviating the polarized views. However, existing methods fail to 1) effectively incorporate the semantic information from content-related posts; 2) preserve the structural information for reply relationship modeling; 3) properly handle posts from topics dissimilar to those in the training set.

arxiv-2101-03739.title: Solvability of a Regular Polynomial Vector Optimization Problem without Convexity Thanks: This work was partially supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China (11471230).
arxiv-2101-03739.creator: Danyang Liu 1, Rong Hu 2, Yaping Fang 1
arxiv-2101-03739.description: Abstract In this paper we consider the solvability of a non-convex regular polynomial vector optimization problem on a nonempty closed set. We introduce regularity conditions for the polynomial vector optimization problem and study properties and characterizations of the regularity conditions. Under the regularity conditions, we study nonemptiness and boundedness of the solution sets of the problem.

arxiv-2201-11656.title: Symmetries in Linear Programming for Information Inequalities
arxiv-2201-11656.creator: Emirhan Gürpınar
arxiv-2201-11656.description: Abstract We study the properties of secret sharing schemes, where a random secret value is transformed into shares distributed among several participants in such a way that only the qualified groups of participants can recover the secret value. We improve the lower bounds on the sizes of shares for several specific problems of secret sharing.

arxiv-2201-13140.title: Polynomial kernels for edge modification problems towards block and strictly chordal graphs Thanks: A preliminary version of this work appeared in IPEC’21 ( 21 ) . All results concerning Block Graph Editing are new to this submission.
arxiv-2201-13140.creator: Maël Dumas, Anthony Perez, Mathis Rocton, Ioan Todinca
arxiv-2201-13140.description: Abstract We consider edge modification problems towards block and strictly chordal graphs, where one is given an undirected graph G = ( V , E ) G=(V,E) and an integer k ∈ ℕ k\in\mathbb{N} and seeks to edit (add or delete) at most k k edges from G G to obtain a block graph or a strictly chordal graph.

arxiv-2303-06862.title: OTOv2: Automatic, Generic, User-Friendly
arxiv-2303-06862.creator: Tianyi Chen, Luming Liang, Tianyu Ding, Ilya Zharkov, Zhihui Zhu
arxiv-2303-06862.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Tianyi Chen, Luming Liang, Tianyu Ding, Ilya Zharkov, Zhihui Zhu. The existing model compression methods via structured pruning typically require complicated multi-stage procedures. Each individual stage necessitates numerous engineering efforts and domain-knowledge from the end-users which prevent their wider applications onto broader scenarios. We propose the second generation of Only-Train-Once (OTOv2), which first automatically trains and compresses a general DNN only once from scratch to produce a more compact model with competitive performance without fine-tuning.

arxiv-2403-07206.title: Non-Standard Version of Egorov Algebra of Generalized Functions
arxiv-2403-07206.creator: Todor D. Todorov
arxiv-2403-07206.description: Abstract . We consider a non-standard version of Egorov’s algebra of generalized functions, with improved properties of the generalized scalars and embedding of the Schwartz distributions compared with the original standard Egorov’s version. The embedding of distributions is similar to, but different from author’s works in the past and independently done by Hans Vernaeve.

arxiv-2409-15786.title: Improving behavior profile discovery for vehicles
arxiv-2409-15786.creator: Nelson de Moura, Fernando Garrido, Fawzi Nashashibi
arxiv-2409-15786.description: Abstract Multiple approaches have already been proposed to mimic real driver behaviors in simulation. This article proposes a new one, based solely on the exploration of undisturbed observation of intersections. From them, the behavior profiles for each macro-maneuver will be discovered.

arxiv-2512-00666.title: Controlling weak-lensing shear biases from undetected galaxies in the era of Stage IV Surveys 2023 Controlling weak-lensing shear biases from undetected galaxies in the era of Stage IV Surveys – B
arxiv-2512-00666.creator: L. M. Voigt
arxiv-2512-00666.description: Abstract Gravitational lensing of background galaxies by intervening matter is a powerful probe of the cosmological model. In the era of Stage IV surveys, contamination from galaxies below the detection threshold has emerged as a significant source of bias. Adopting a noise-bias-free machine-learning method to estimate shear, we quantify the impact of faint galaxies for a Euclid-like survey.

arxiv-2512-06152.title: A Landau Theory for Pair Density Modulation in Fe(Te,Se) flakes.
arxiv-2512-06152.creator: Po-Jui Chen, Piers Coleman
arxiv-2512-06152.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Po-Jui Chen, Piers Coleman. Motivated by recent scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) experiments reporting a pair-density modulation (PDM) in FeTe 0.55 Se 0.45 , we develop a Landau theory to elucidate the physical origin of this phenomenon. We analyze the PDM in terms of the screw symmetry of the single layer, interpreting it as a hybridized state of two order parameters of opposite glide and screw parity.

arxiv-2601-16378.title: Cognitively-Inspired Tokens Overcome Egocentric Bias in Multimodal Models
arxiv-2601-16378.creator: Bridget Leonard, Scott O. Murray
arxiv-2601-16378.description: Abstract Multimodal language models (MLMs) perform well on semantic vision–language tasks but fail at spatial reasoning that requires adopting another agent’s visual perspective. These errors reflect a persistent egocentric bias and raise questions about whether current models support allocentric reasoning.

arxiv-2602-11149.title: Data Repetition Beats Data Scaling in Long-CoT Supervised Fine-Tuning
arxiv-2602-11149.creator: Dawid J. Kopiczko, Sagar Vaze, Tijmen Blankevoort, Yuki M. Asano
arxiv-2602-11149.description: Abstract Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on chain-of-thought data is an essential post-training step for reasoning language models. Standard machine learning intuition suggests that training with more unique training samples yields better generalization. Counterintuitively, we show that SFT benefits from repetition : under a fixed update budget, training for more epochs on smaller datasets outperforms single-epoch training on larger datasets.

arxiv-2602-19075.title: Gravitational Baryogenesis in f ⁡ ( R ) f(R) Cosmologies
arxiv-2602-19075.creator: Ian B. Whittingham
arxiv-2602-19075.description: Abstract The origin of the small asymmetry in the abundance of matter and antimatter in the very early universe, described by the Baryon Asymmetry Factor η = 8.65 × 10 − 11 \eta=8.65\times 10^{-11} , is one of the big unanswered questions of contemporary physics.

arxiv-2604-16418.title: Towards Solving NP-Complete and Other Hard Problems Efficiently in Practice Journal: Theoretical Computer Science
arxiv-2604-16418.creator: Mircea-Adrian Digulescu

doe-osti-2589062-develop-a-new-integrate.creator: Hu, Xiaohua, Freiberg, Daniel, Huo, Yang et al.
doe-osti-2589062-develop-a-new-integrate.description: U.S. Department of Energy technical report. Bending tests provide a means to study plane strain fracture performance of 6000 series aluminum alloys. Metrics from bending tests have been correlated with self-pierce riveting (SPR) performance of a high strength AA6111 automotive aluminum alloy in previous works. Using the OR

pmc-10573487.title: Carbon Dots—Types, Obtaining and Application in Biotechnology and Food Technology
pmc-10573487.creator: Joanna Szczepankowska, Gohar Khachatryan, Karen Khachatryan, Magdalena Krystyjan, Ilaria Armentano
pmc-10573487.description: Materials with a “nano” structure are increasingly used in medicine and biotechnology as drug delivery systems, bioimaging agents or biosensors in the monitoring of toxic substances, heavy metals and environmental variations. Furthermore, in the food industry, they have found applications as detectors of food adulteration, microbial contamination and even in packaging for monitoring product freshness.

pmc-10619240.title: Efficacy and safety of traditional Chinese medicine for cancer-related fatigue: a systematic literature review of randomized controlled trials
pmc-10619240.creator: Jingya Yang, Yuxiao Li, Chi Ian Chau, Junnan Shi, Xianwen Chen, Hao Hu, Carolina Oi Lam Ung
pmc-10619240.description: BackgroundCancer-related fatigue (CRF) is an extremely common and long-term condition that affects the physical and mental health of oncology patients. While the treatment for CRF with western medicine and non-pharmacological therapy remains uncertain and challenging, traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) has become a trending option for the patients.

pmc-10624727.title: Alcohol-Associated Liver Disease: Evolving Concepts and Treatments
pmc-10624727.creator: David Stephen Prince, Emily Nash, Ken Liu
pmc-10624727.description: Alcohol is a prominent cause of liver disease worldwide with higher prevalence in developed nations. The spectrum of alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) encompasses a diverse range of clinical entities, from asymptomatic isolated steatosis to decompensated cirrhosis, and in some cases, acute or chronic liver failure. Consequently, it is important for healthcare practitioners to maintain awareness and systematically screen for ALD.

pmc-10928982.title: African Global Health: An initiative committed to achieving Health Sovereignty in the Global South
pmc-10928982.creator: MORGAN CHETTY, ENRIQUE TERAN, LUWAGA PATRICK, RANIA MAMDOUH, SUNITHA CHANDRASEKHHAR SRINIVAS, JEAN KASEYA, NICAISE NDEMBI, SARA TOUIRSI, IMANE KENDILI
pmc-10928982.description: has exposed vulnerabilities in health systems, especially in Africa, and underscored the critical need for sovereign health systems to address the continent's unique challenges. The concept of sovereign health systems has recently gained prominence in global health discourse by focussing on the right to self-determination and independence of control over its health systems, Policies and Programs.

pmc-11444524.title: The Effect of Long-Term Particulate Matter Exposure on Respiratory Mortality: Cohort Study in China
pmc-11444524.creator: Ying Wang, Zhuohao Wang, Jie Jiang, Tong Guo, Shimin Chen, Zhiqiang Li, Zhupei Yuan, Qiaoxuan Lin, Zhicheng Du, Jing Wei, Yuantao Hao, Wangjian Zhang
pmc-11444524.description: BackgroundParticulate matter (PM), which affects respiratory health, has been well documented; however, substantial evidence from large cohorts is still limited, particularly in highly polluted countries and for PM1.ObjectiveOur objective was to examine the potential causal links between long-term exposure to PMs (PM2.5, PM10, and more importantly, PM1) and respiratory mortality.

pmc-11687677.title: Oropharyngeal Colostrum Administration in Premature Infants: Impact on Immune Status and Incidence of Common Morbidities
pmc-11687677.creator: Majid Mohammadizadeh, Azadeh Jafari, Behzad Barekatain
pmc-11687677.description: Background:Enteral feeding of preterm infants with maternal colostrum has well-known effects on protecting them, especially against serious infections. This study was conducted to determine whether oropharyngeal administration of colostrum to these infants, soon after birth, has any additional effect on their clinical outcomes and stimulation of their immune system.

pmc-11688759.title: IMPLEMENTATION BOOSTER: TESTING A VIRTUAL SIMULATION GAME TO ENHANCE CONFIDENCE AND COMPETENCE
pmc-11688759.creator: Grace Armstrong, Mary McCormack, Ilona Seaman, Mary Dolansky, Anne Pohnert, Nicholas Schiltz, Sarah Ball
pmc-11688759.description: The Virtual Clinic, a serious video game, aimed to improve provider competency and confidence in the delivery of AFHS 4Ms care through simulation of realistic older adult patient visits. The Virtual Clinic (VC) was developed in response to focus groups of front-line providers that revealed they valued gaining competency in delivering 4Ms through practice.

pmc-12407474.title: Adaptive force-position-speed collaborative process planning and roughness prediction for robotic polishing
pmc-12407474.creator: Ma Haohao, Azizan As’arry, Niu Jing, Mohd Idris Shah Ismail, Hafiz Rashidi Ramli, M. Y. M. Zuhri, Aidin Delgoshaei, Carlos Alberto Cruz-Villar, Carlos Alberto Cruz-Villar, Carlos Alberto Cruz-Villar, Carlos Alberto Cruz-Villar
pmc-12407474.description: In this study, an adaptive force-position-speed collaborative process planning framework for robot polishing was proposed to improve the stability of the robot polishing process. The material removal model based on Preston’s theory was studied, and the factors of polishing pressure, tool speed, feed speed, and sandpaper type were considered to design the manual polishing experiment.

pmc-12433235.title: Prioritising the Burden of Geographic Atrophy and Treatment Expectations: A Modified Nominal Group Technique Study with International Patient-Led Organisations
pmc-12433235.creator: Nabin Paudel, Ellen M Moran, Sinead Stafford, Kelly McVicker, Petia Stratieva, Avril Daly
pmc-12433235.description: AimGeographic atrophy (GA), an advanced form of dry AMD, impacts over 5 million people globally and leads to progressive, irreversible vision loss. Current approaches to GA treatment aim to prevent and delay disease progression and preserve remaining vision. However, there is a debate on what constitutes a meaningful treatment outcome for patients.

pmc-12665234.title: Clinical and Genomic Characteristics of Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae Bloodstream Infections in Older Adults: A Single-Center Study from Changsha, China
pmc-12665234.creator: Fang Qin, Yanjun Liu, Zijuan Jian, Qun Yan, Wenen Liu
pmc-12665234.description: BackgroundBloodstream infections (BSIs) caused by carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) pose a huge threat to global public health. The mortality rates are particularly high among older adults. However, few studies have focused on CRKP BSIs in older adults. This study aims to investigate the clinical and genomic characteristics of CRKP-BSIs in older adults.

pmc-12947657.title: A Network Meta-Analysis Comparing the Efficacy Differences of Different Acupuncture and Sodium Hyaluronate Eye Drops in the Treatment of Dry Eye Disease
pmc-12947657.creator: Xin Yan, Jinlu Hu, Yuxin Chen, Shiqi Lei, Jing Chen, Mu Qin
pmc-12947657.description: ObjectiveTo systematically evaluate the efficacy of different acupuncture methods and sodium hyaluronate eye drops in the treatment of dry eye disease, and to rank the interventions through a network meta-analysis.MethodsChinese and English databases were searched to collect randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published from the establishment of the databases to October 14, 2025.

pmc-12965565.title: Integrating contrastive cross-modal attention and stacked GRU for hand function rehabilitation robot control
pmc-12965565.creator: Wei Liu, Huidong Wu, Shi-Fu Feng, Chang-Liang Luo
pmc-12965565.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). With the intensification of population aging and the increasing incidence of neurological diseases, the demand for precise and intelligent control technology in hand rehabilitation robots has become more urgent. Traditional control methods struggle to effectively capture the dynamic temporal features of hand movements, especially in scenarios where there are modal differences between hand function data of healthy individuals and stroke patients, leading to insufficient control accuracy and poor generalization.

pmc-13049402.title: Cohort design transparency is crucial for TriNetX-based studies
pmc-13049402.creator: Joshua Wang
pmc-13049402.description: and state that the codes used to construct their cohorts are available in their attached Appendix. However, this file does not define any of the clinical codes used. Furthermore, the temporal relationship between the inclusion and exclusion criteria for each cohort is not well-defined. These details can greatly influence the findings of TriNetX-based studies.

pmc-13321391.title: Mid-Year Roundup: So You are Saying There’s a Chance…
pmc-13321391.creator: Brett R. Levine

pmc-13422874.title: Structural analysis of recombinant AAV vector genomes at single-molecule resolution
pmc-13422874.creator: David Rouleau, Dimpal Lata, Serena Dollive, Robert E. Bruccoleri, Laura Van Lieshout, Diane Golebiowski, Ifeyinwa Iwuchukwu
pmc-13422874.description: Recombinant adeno-associated virus vectors are essential tools for in vivo gene therapy, yet heterogeneity in their packaged genomes remains an important safety consideration. To systematically evaluate this heterogeneity, we developed a long-read, read-level analysis pipeline that directly classifies individual AAV genomes and their structural variants from PacBio sequencing data.

pmc-13457593.title: Extracting the transitivity backbone of bipartite networks
pmc-13457593.creator: Lucía S. Ramirez, Roya Aliakbarisani, M. Ángeles Serrano, Marián Boguñá
pmc-13457593.description: Real bipartite networks combine degree-constrained random mixing with structured connectivity balancing short and long range connections, effectively accounted for by geometric network models. We introduce a statistical filter that benchmarks node-level bipartite clustering against degree-preserving randomizations to classify nodes as geometric (signal) or degree constrained noise.

pmc-13634512.title: Body-weight variation as a potential indirect indicator of abdominal fat weight with relevance to laying rate in 90-week-old laying hens
pmc-13634512.creator: Alexandre Hubert, Nicolas Bedere, Fabien Degalez, Coralie Allain, Lorry Becot, Quentin Berger, Thierry Burlot, Mathieu Emily, Alexandre Ferry, Laetitia Lagoutte, Bénédicte Lebez, Marie-Pierre Sanchez, Thierry Tribout, Frédérique Pitel, Tatiana Zerjal, Sophie Allais, Sandrine Lagarrigue
pmc-13634512.description: In livestock species, efficient regulation of body lipid reserves contributes to prolonged reproductive performance, as shown in dairy cattle and more recently in laying hens through abdominal fat reserves. Controlling abdominal fat weight (AFW) at 90 weeks may improve metabolic efficiency and late egg production. However, AFW measurement requires slaughter and dissection, preventing routine use.
